definition: VXL, the Vision-something-Library, is a large collection of open source C++ libraries for computer vision.
details: The idea of the naming is to replace X with one of many letters to obtain the smaller library names, i.e. G (VGL) is a geometry library, N (VNL) is a numerics library, I (VIL) is an image processing library, etc. These libraries can be used for general scientific computing as well as computer vision. Some examples of usage can be seen online. VXL is a larger-scale software engineering project with roots dating back to traditional computer vision environments from the 1990s, having libraries at multiple levels of complexities, many of them listing OpenCV as one of many dependencies. A similar approach at an even larger scale is taken by Kitware's KWIVER. VXL core libraries are extremely stable and have been used in larger projects, both public and within companies, notably ITK.

explainer.lead: VXL is a large collection of open source C++ libraries for computer vision. Its naming swaps X for letters that denote smaller libraries, such as VGL for geometry, VNL for numerics, and VIL for image processing.

tiers.eli5: It is a big toolbox of C++ parts for building vision software, with each drawer named after the letter that tells you what is inside.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the libraries for computer vision and general scientific computing. A pitfall is that the many constituent libraries mean dependency choices need care.
tiers.paperLevel: A large-scale open source C++ library collection for computer vision and scientific computing, with roots in 1990s traditional computer vision environments; sub-libraries are named by substituting X (e.g., G, N, I).

explainer.example: A project needing geometry, numerics, and image processing could draw on VGL, VNL, and VIL respectively from the same collection.
